method: scripts/sealed-boot/measure: alternating paired cold `bl run` of (println 1) through the SDK's own boot path (boot-at.exs). O = the SDK itself; C = scratch copy, unchanged hosts (control); L = scratch copy with the branch's edited hosts (application.bl, env.bl, aot.bl, package_authority.bl) compiled by the SDK's compiler, restamped, image-metadata resealed (scripts/sealed-boot/build-image ... image-metadata). Not an SDK: priv/std/proc/owner-registry.bl is the SDK's own in L.

baseline_profile.how: call-timeline tracer (return_trace on chosen host functions) + deep-stack sampler, 1 run each on the SDK
baseline_profile.experiment: same SDK, app start by hand without the owner registry child: 2,372 -> 1,518 / 2,408 -> 1,592 / 2,118 -> 1,342 ms paired (load 15-18)

changes: Application start no longer loads or starts proc.owner-registry; Env/ensure_sdk_owner_registry! loads and starts it (fresh process, same supervisor) for the first managed actor; proc.owner-registry/page starts a never-started collector instead of answering :unavailable

No SDK lease at app start. The lease is established by its existing on-demand callers (ensure_sdk_runtime! from generation prepare/ward/build/execution, prepare_sdk_class!, adopt_*), and sdk_runtime_retained_modules? establishes a never-taken lease for a native adapter (outside Source, outside the Env owner, outside held publication/capacity fences, in a fresh process)

First lease after many pre-lease loads: complete_image_sdk_closure! walks metadata, then loads the selected members in one code:ensure_modules_loaded batch; the first loader batch after the lease also plans the requires of namespaces loaded before it (one lease extension instead of ~12)

Pre-lease image namespace loads publish the sealed image's complete-unit rows (artifact sha256 vs inventory row, Source digest, complete-unit check, loaded MD5) instead of recovering them through the per-user AOT cache
Once per VM on a root that resolves into /nix/store: sdk-code.term bytes (3.5 MB, ~35 reads), the sealed image table path, the preinit floor's seed/host directory stamps
package_module_identity loads a compiler dependency from the code path before fingerprinting it (the eager lease's closure walk used to have loaded it)

first_actor_path.probe: bl run of a file that prepares a generation, snapshots its inventory, starts a managed defserver and pings it
first_actor_path.note: without the batched closure load and deferred-require planning the first lease cost +6.7 s; with them it is level with the eager lease

measured.summary: cold bl run 2,159 -> 1,170 ms median (-46%) against the unchanged SDK, 6 alternating pairs at load ~18-22; the :beam_lisp app start 1,405 -> 552 ms

tests_on_scratch_images.how: cold `bl test` through boot-at.exs on L and C, cwd a scratch copy of test/ and priv/host (no env.bl)
tests_on_scratch_images.ten_files_L9: realm_package fixed by the package_authority change (112 passed); the other nine passed on L7/L8
tests_on_scratch_images.seed_and_aot_74_files: L8: 69 passed, 5 failed; C: 70 passed, 4 failed. The 4 shared failures are the scratch cwd (no build/, no research/, no reader source). The extra L failure, aot_implicit_dependencies, is the harness: its child runs the SDK's own bin/bl, whose Env/AOT md5 differ from the overlaid hosts
tests_on_scratch_images.owner/host tests: native_owner_registry_start, host_application (except a surface check: the harness compiles application.bl without :behaviour), host_supervisor, host_loader_server, cli_application_startup pass on L7; the four that encode the new start fail on C, as they should
